append.text: **Ps 106 refrain (106:8, 15, 21, 31) *Confiteántur Dómino misericórdiæ ejus: et mirabília ejus fíliis hóminum* → *Que as suas misericórdias deem graças ao Senhor: * e as suas maravilhas, aos filhos dos homens*** — D5 applied; *misericórdiæ* is nominative (not *misericórdias*), so the mercies are the subject (DRB); MS1932's *pelas suas misericórdias* (the Hebrew) refused. The Latinist confirmed it twice; the blind reader found it strange, as the Latin is. Options: the Latin's order (*Que deem graças ao Senhor as suas misericórdias*), DRB's *Que as misericórdias do Senhor lhe deem graças*. See the formula row.
Ps 106:2 *qui redémpti sunt … quos redémit* → *os resgatados … os que ele resgatou* — the row applied; *remidos … remiu* option.

**Ps 106:4 *Erravérunt in solitúdine* → *Extraviaram-se na solidão*** — the named test passed: kept apart from desértum (*deserto*, 106:33, 35); no reader objected (the blind reader heard the place, some also the state).

**Ps 106:4, 7, 36 (habitáculi / habitatiónis / habitatiónis, one Greek κατοικητήριον at 4 and 7) → *uma cidade onde morar*, all three** (v2): D15's test lets the psalm's echo stand in one word; draft 1 *cidade de morada* was failed by the stylist three times as a calque, so the genitive of purpose became a clause (D2) with *morar* keeping the root. Option: *de morada* / *de habitação*.
Ps 106:7, 36 *civitátem habitatiónis* (a city for men) → *uma cidade onde morar*, with 106:4's habitáculi — see the habitáculum row; the row's *habitação* was an option.
**Ps 106:6, 13, 19, 28 *cum tribularéntur* → *quando estavam atribulados*** (the second refrain, one slot) — the verb kept; *na sua tribulação* (DRB, MS1932) option.
Ps 106:6, 20 *erípuit eos de …* → *os arrancou de* — kept apart from liberávit (*livrou*, 106:13, 19) and edúxit (*tirou*, 106:28), as the Latin varies the refrain's verb.

**Ps 106:6, 13, 19, 28 → *das suas necessidades*** — the row applied at its named places (the straits here are hunger, prison, sickness, storm); the blind reader heard 'needs / hardships'; *angústias* option.

**Ps 106:11 *exacerbavérunt elóquia Dei … irritavérunt* → *exasperaram as palavras de Deus … provocaram*** — D27 applied: two Greek verbs (παρεπίκραναν / παρώξυναν), so irritáre keeps *provocar* and exacerbáre takes *exasperar* (L&S, DRB). One blind reader did not know it. *amarguraram* option (Ps 105:32 chose it — **the two psalms differ; for Gustavo**).

**Ps 106:11 *elóquia Dei* → *as palavras de Deus*** (v2, D26: the psalm decides) — draft 1 had D26's clause *o que Deus disse* to keep it apart from 106:20 *verbum* (*a sua palavra*); the Latinist and the stylist both asked for the plural noun, as 11:7. The merge with verbum nine verses off accepted.

**Ps 106:17 *Suscépit eos de via iniquitátis eórum* → *Recolheu-os do caminho*** — a local departure from D19: with a source (*de via*), *amparar de* is not Portuguese; *recolher* is 'take up' from the road. No reader objected. Options *Amparou-os, fora*, *Tirou-os*.
Ps 106:20 *de interitiónibus eórum* (interítio, plural) → *da sua destruição* — the singular (D2); the Latinist asked the plural twice (minor), held as the option *das suas destruições*.
**Ps 106:27 *moti sunt sicut ébrius* → *vacilaram como um ébrio*** — the row's option taken beside the drunkard; *ébrio* not *bêbado* (a proparoxytone at the mediant).
Ps 106:29 *státuit procéllam ejus in auram* → *fez da sua tempestade uma brisa* — *firmar* unreadable here; options *mudou … em*, *assentou*.

**Ps 106:38 *juménta eórum non minorávit* → *não diminuiu os seus animais*** — the row applied (plural herds, no animália in the psalm); the Latinist asked *jumentos*, the stylist *gado*: both refused (v1).
Ps 106:38 *multiplicáti sunt nimis* → *se multiplicaram sem medida* (as 118:138, 78:8).
**Ps 106:40 *in ínvio, et non in via* → *no lugar sem caminho, e não no caminho*** — the row applied, built like 106:4 *no lugar sem água* (in inaquóso).

**Ps 106:41 *adjúvit páuperem de inópia* → *auxiliou o pobre a sair da penúria*** (v2) — *penúria* applied; draft 1 *na penúria* (59:13's *na*) was heard as static by the Latinist and the stylist (de = out of); *sair* supplied. The ambiguity reader did not know *penúria*.

**Ps 106:32 *in cáthedra seniórum* → *na cátedra dos anciãos*** (v2) — the row's *cadeira* was tried at its named test and failed: the stylist and the blind reader both heard a piece of furniture (the elders sharing one chair). The verse is the Gradual of the Chair of St Peter, in Brazil *Cátedra de São Pedro*. 1:1 unaffected. **Proposed: cáthedra of a seat of authority → *cátedra*.**

terms: | mendícitas | pobreza (*presos na pobreza e no ferro*) | open | Ps 106:10 only (grep); the Greek πτωχεία is the noun of πτωχός (pauper → pobre). Draft 1 *mendicância* (mendícus's root) failed the stylist (bookish) and the blind reader (unknown); *miséria* refused as misería's. |

| vectis | tranca (*as trancas de ferro*) | open | Ps 106:16 (μοχλός), beside contérere / confríngere (*quebrou … despedaçou*, 45:10). *ferrolhos* (MS1932) option — *ferrolhos de ferro* jingles. One blind reader did not know *trancas*; kept. 147:13 *seras portárum* is another word. |
| salsúgo | sal (*a terra frutífera em sal*) | open | Ps 106:34 only. The Latinist asked *salsugem* twice (minor), held as option: rare in Brazil; the land turned to salt is the image. |

| fructus nativitátis | *fizeram nascer fruto* | open | Ps 106:37 (καρπὸν γενήματος); the genitive made a verb so both Latin words stay; the Latinist asked *fruto de nascimento* twice (minor), held as option (opaque). |

| pónere … in (turn into) | tornar … em (*Tornou os rios em deserto*) | open | Ps 106:33, 35 (ἔθετο εἰς): *pôs … em* is heard as placing (rivers put in a desert — a blessing). Kept apart from convértere in (*converter em*). 106:41 *pósuit sicut oves* keeps *pôs … como*. |
| oppiláre | tapar (*toda iniquidade tapará a sua boca*) | open | Ps 106:42 (L&S 'stop up'; MS1932 *fechará*). 62:12 *obstrúctum est os* is another verb. |
| stagna aquárum | lagoas de água | open | Ps 106:35 (λίμνας); 113:8 *in stagna aquárum* should copy. *tanques* (MS1932) are tanks in Brazil. |

| Dicant (with no object, after a formula) | *Que o digam* (*Que o digam os resgatados pelo Senhor*) | open | Ps 106:2 (after 106:1 = 117:1). 117:2–4 *Dicat nunc Israel* has a quotation after it — a different build. *Digam-no* (MS1932) option. |
formulas: | *Confiteántur Dómino misericórdiæ ejus: * et mirabília ejus fíliis hóminum* (106:8 = 15 = 21 = 31; Gradual / Alleluia verse — missa Epi2-0, Sancti 02-22, 06-30, 10-20, Commune Coronatio, horas C4b) | *Que as suas misericórdias deem graças ao Senhor: * e as suas maravilhas, aos filhos dos homens* | open — Ps 106 (v2); misericórdiæ nominative, the subject (DRB); see the confitéri row. |

| *Et clamavérunt ad Dóminum cum tribularéntur: * et de necessitátibus eórum …* (106:6 = 13 = 19 = 28, the verb varying) | *E clamaram ao Senhor quando estavam atribulados: * e ele os arrancou (erípuit) / livrou (liberávit) / tirou (edúxit) das suas necessidades* | open — Ps 106 (v2); the first colon identical four times; the second varies with the Latin verb. |

| *Exáltent eum in ecclésia plebis: * et in cáthedra seniórum laudent eum* (106:32 without *Et*; the Gradual of St Peter's Chair, missa Sancti 02-22, and of the Common of Popes, C4b, Coronatio; V. *Exáltent eum in Ecclésia plebis*) | *Exaltem-no na assembleia do povo: * e o louvem na cátedra dos anciãos* | open — Ps 106 (v2); read alone; in the psalm *E o exaltem*. |
| *Misit verbum suum, et sanávit eos* (106:20a; Matins versicle, Psalterium/Special/Matutinum Special) | *Enviou a sua palavra, e os curou* | open — Ps 106 (v2); reads alone unchanged. |
